subject: Re: Summit Bank RFP — failover scenarios and DR dry-run details
content:

Subject: Summit Bank RFP — clarifications on RTO/RPO and dry-run requirements

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick turn on the RFP submission. Our security/ops review team has two follow-ups before we move to the procurement redlines:

1) Can Redwood confirm typical and worst-case RTO and RPO for multi-region failover for a single-tenant (dedicated) deployment, and how these change with active KV cache warming?
2) We require a customer-observable dry-run (non-disruptive) test plan for failover — can you provide a proposed checklist, estimated windows, and any blackout periods?
3) For legal: evidence of controlled failback and post-failover data consistency checks (we will need a runbook excerpt).

We are targeting a security review completion by EOD Feb 15. Can you respond with specifics and any supporting artifacts?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior IT Procurement
Summit Bank

--- Message 2 of 4 ---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@summitbank.com>
Cc: Naveen Patel <naveen.patel@summitbank.com>, itprocurement@summitbank.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Summit Bank RFP — clarifications on RTO/RPO and dry-run requirements

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are three artifacts that should cover the questions at a high level: Redwood_DR_Executive_Summary.pdf (executive RTO/RPO commitments), summit-failover-diagram.png (sequence diagram), and dry-run-checklist.xlsx (proposed non-disruptive test plan). High-level answers below; Karthik will add technical detail in a follow-up.

RTO / RPO (Dedicated pools, multi-region):
- Typical (expected): RTO = 3–7 minutes for services with warm KV cache + routing (automated prefix cache restoration); RPO = 0–30 seconds for session-level state when KV cache is replicated asynchronously with per-region checkpointing.
- Worst-case (cold start, full region loss): RTO = 20–35 minutes depending on dataset size and model weights transfer/quantized image availability; RPO = up to 5 minutes if requests in-flight are lost and must be replayed from client-side logs.

Notes: these numbers assume the customer uses Redwood Dedicated with our cross-region replica policy and enables snapshot replication (recommended for PCI/finance customers). We provide configurable cache-warming policies (auto-prefetch from snapshot + request-replay seeding) to reduce warm-up time.

Dry-run (non-disruptive) approach:
- Objective: validate orchestration, routing policies, and telemetry without interrupting live traffic.
- Proposed window: 60–90 minutes for a single dry-run; full rehearsal across critical flows may take 3–4 hours depending on traffic shaping.
- Steps: traffic mirroring to the target region, canary routing for 5% of test tenants, verification of trace continuity and token/cost accounting, simulated failback sequence. See dry-run-checklist.xlsx.

Evidence and runbook excerpt: attached PDF includes the controlled failback sequence and post-failover data consistency checks (hash comparisons for persisted KV snapshots, reconciliation job templates). Legal/ops teams can redact items as needed.

Next steps: Karthik can provide the low-level sequencing (model weights transfer, registry integrity checks, and delta-snapshot choreography). Also looping Marcus to propose a dry-run date range and resource requirements.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DR_Executive_Summary.pdf (3 pages), summit-failover-diagram.png (1 image), dry-run-checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: Summit Bank RFP — clarifications on RTO/RPO and dry-run requirements

Elena — quick technical addendum below.

1) Cache warming and KV strategy:
- We support both synchronous and asynchronous checkpoint replication. For near-zero RPO, customers use synchronous snapshot commits to object store with cross-region replication turned on. That yields RPO < 1s for persisted state but increases write latency; we can provide latency profiles in the SLO appendix.
- Our warm-up process uses prioritized prefix seeding + progressive KV fetches; for very large models we ship quantized weights images to each region in advance (customer can opt for pre-staged images to guarantee sub-10 minute model availability).

2) Model weight transfer and cold start mitigation:
- Typical image transfer (compressed quantized artifact) between regions over private backbone: 30–180 seconds per GB depending on link; we recommend pre-staging for models >10GB.
- For extreme worst-case recovery, we support streaming checkpoint replay which allows inference to resume at reduced throughput while weights finish transferring.

3) Dry-run technical controls:
- Non-disruptive mirroring uses our traffic-split primitives; we never flip the primary DNS in a dry-run.
- Observability hooks: automatic side-by-side traces, token-usage divergence reports, and cost delta estimates. We can produce a signed test report.

If Summit wants, we can include an optional canary policy that rolls internal test tenants through failover to validate stateful sessions.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

- Option B: Thu Mar 9, 21:00–23:00 (off-hours)

- Decide whether you want pre-staged model images for the target region (recomm. for models >5GB).

If those dates work we will provision a temporary canary tenant and provide a signed test report within 24 hours of completion. If legal needs a redlined runbook excerpt for doc retention, Tom, loop in your counsel and we can prepare a version with limited internal-only detail.
